title: Web intelligence: Firecrawl-compatible scrape, search and extract, browser-free fetch, and the isolated Firecrawl component

dependency_notes.SG-000131: Contracts, audit chain, licence and provenance gates (the AGPL carve-out for apps/orcel-firecrawl).
dependency_notes.SG-000040: Closed. The Windows WinHTTP transport with DNS pinning and the exact-peer check is reused; this grain amends its 'no MCP network tool' and 'no caller headers' rules for exactly the shapes listed here, and extends the transport to macOS and Linux (WP1-13).
dependency_notes.SG-000064: Closed. Admitted web_fetch; its network-tool guard tests are amended here.
dependency_notes.SG-000108: Closed. Governed navigation, extraction and the test fixture pinning used by the chromium engine and the harness.

objective: Deliver Firecrawl feature parity, copy first (FD-UP-1): an Apache-2.0 contract layer (crates/orcel-web, orceld dispatch, MCP tools and loopback REST routes for Firecrawl v2 natively and v1 where practical) over a browser-free fetch engine (governed fetch, Windows first, macOS and Linux in parallel) and an isolated AGPL-3.0 component apps/orcel-firecrawl holding copied Firecrawl code (html.rs, markdown.rs, crawler.rs, xml.rs, utils.rs in Wave 1; the extract pipeline in Wave 2) run under orcel-contain with no network, no process creation and a JSON-over-stdio protocol, with upstream licence, notices, provenance and a source offer. Scrape and search in Wave 1; extract, structured outputs, document parsing and the remaining rows in Wave 2. Custom request headers (credentials from the OS secret store, per-client permission, destination-scoped, redacted) and the sensitive-feature policy gate (privacy defaults on; fingerprint, TLS impersonation, proxy, geo and device emulation off by default, per-client permission, audited; no security bypass). No Firecrawl Cloud dependency. Spec sections 4.11, 4.12, 4.16, 4.17, 5, 6, 8.2 and 8.3.

include: WP1-05: crates/orcel-web (v2, v1, refusals, translation, Document shaping, status mapping, policy fields).

WP1-08: apps/orcel-firecrawl (own workspace, AGPL-3.0, LICENSE, NOTICE, PROVENANCE.json pinned to firecrawl/firecrawl@42f4d669954649ce33466a2a50e8215c7f1f4d1c, PATCHES.md, deny.toml) with copied src/upstream/{html,markdown,crawler,xml,utils}.rs; contained launch entry; crates/orceld/src/web_fetch_engine.rs; separate release package with source archive.
WP1-06 (scrape, search): web/scrape and web/search dispatch; one SOFT approval per scrape bound to URL, engine, formats, resolved addresses, client and session; capability entries per OS and build.

WP1-07: tool_contract entry web_scrape; REST routes /v2/scrape, /v1/scrape, /v2/search, /v1/search; per-client REST tokens created and rotated with SOFT approval; network-tool guard amendment for the eight web tools.
WP1-09: tests/firecrawl-compat with @mendable/firecrawl-js 4.54.0 and firecrawl-py 4.57.0 (CI only) against the pinned fixture site.
WP1-13 (track X): macOS and Linux HTTPS transport (rustls with the platform verifier, DNS pinning, exact-peer check) and the SG-000040 amendment for those OSes.
WP1-16: credential headers (OS secret store, destination binding, dropped on cross-origin redirect, redaction) and the sensitive-feature gate with per-client permissions.

WP2-13 (Wave 2, same grain): the copied extract pipeline (apps/api/src/lib/extract, excluding Redis and cloud paths) on the pinned Node runtime inside the component, model calls proxied by orceld from the user's configured provider, structured outputs validated against the schema; /v2/extract, json and summary formats; /v2/parse through the document parser.
exclude: Any AGPL code in crates/* or the Apache apps; any link between an Apache unit and the component.
Firecrawl cloud-only features and any Firecrawl Cloud dependency.
CAPTCHA solving, login, paywall or access-control bypass, ignoring robots rules, skipTlsVerification.
Remote (relay or OAuth) exposure of the web tools.

authority_delta.web: Proposed: local-only web/scrape and web/search shapes composing the governed transport and the contained component behind one SOFT approval per request; caller headers only under per-client permission with credentials from the OS secret store; sensitive privacy features only under per-client permission.
authority_delta.network_transport: Proposed: the SG-000040 transport on macOS and Linux (WP1-13), with the same pinning and peer rules.
authority_delta.component: Proposed: a contained, network-less AGPL component; it holds no authority.

decisions.question: Firecrawl approach
decisions.status: DECIDED (founder, 2026-11-17, FD-UP-1): full parity, copy first; isolated AGPL component; founder attestation recorded separately.

decisions.question: Sensitive features
decisions.status: DECIDED (FD-UP-2): opt-in, off by default, per-client permission, audited, no security bypass.

decisions.question: Release and platforms
decisions.status: DECIDED (FD-UP-7, FD-UP-12): release once qualified, Windows first, macOS and Linux transport in parallel now.

decisions.question: Headers
decisions.status: DECIDED (FD-UP-8): supported with OS secret storage, per-client permission, destination scoping, redaction.

invariants: orceld remains the sole authority; fronts and the component decide nothing.
AGPL code exists only under apps/orcel-firecrawl and the FD-06 paths; the component ships separately with its source.
The component has no network, no process creation and no file access beyond its private input.
Every refused field is refused before dispatch, by name.
Credential header values never appear in logs, audit, errors or approvals, and are never sent outside their destination origins.
Sensitive features are off unless the calling client holds the permission; every use is audited.
The engine that ran is named in every result and audit record; fallback is never silent.
Safe-mode approvals for pre-existing shapes are unchanged.
acceptance: Every W1 scrape and search row of the parity matrix passes both SDK legs on Windows, and on macOS and Linux once WP1-13 lands; until then those OSes report unsupported.
The component's output equals the upstream fixtures for main content, tag filters, links, metadata and sitemaps.
An approval cannot be replayed after the address set changes or after a restart.
A header secret is refused for an origin outside its binding and dropped on a cross-origin redirect.
A sensitive feature without the client permission fails PERMISSION_REQUIRED; with it, the use is audited.
Licence gates: AGPL markers only in the component and FD-06 paths; the component release archive includes its source.
A fresh-context security judge passes WP1-06, WP1-07, WP1-13 and WP1-16.
